description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs lines 838-839: PolicyNode.qualifier_set is annotated #[allow(dead_code)] because it is stored but never read. The comment says 'Stored for completeness per RFC 5280 §6.1.2(a) but not currently inspected'.

#[allow(dead_code)] on a struct field is a code smell in production code — it suppresses a warning for a field that is allocated and written on every policy tree node but serves no runtime purpose. Two better approaches:

1. Remove the field and the #[allow(dead_code)] for v0.1 (store nothing until it is needed). The field can be added back when qualifier enforcement is implemented.
2. If it must be retained for a future API, document it with a cfg(feature) gate or a TODO in a tracking issue, not a lint suppression.

The current suppression makes auditors spend time on a field that does nothing. It also means PolicyNode carries a Vec<PolicyQualifierInfo> per node that is never freed until the whole tree drops — wasted allocation.
title: ValidationPolicy: allow(dead_code) on qualifier_set field signals unfinished abstraction
